provenance.citation: A. Aamodt, E. Plaza (1994). Case-Based Reasoning: Foundational Issues, Methodological Variations, and System Approaches. AI Communications, IOS Press, Vol. 7, No. 1, pp. 39–59.
provenance.locus: §1.2 (p. 2) illustrative vignettes; §3 / Figure 1 (p. 8) CBR cycle (Retrieve, Reuse, Revise, Retain). No numeric case table appears in the paper; cases below are adapted from the three concrete vignettes the authors use to introduce CBR.
provenance.notes: The paper (Aamodt & Plaza 1994) contains NO numeric case table or feature-vector example in §2–3. It defines the CBR cycle abstractly via Figure 1 (p. 8: Retrieve → Reuse → Revise → Retain) and introduces CBR through three narrative vignettes on p. 2: (1) physician reminded of a patient treated two weeks prior by similarity of symptoms; (2) drilling engineer reminded of past blowout situations by combination of critical measurements; (3) financial consultant reminded of a previous troubled company when deciding on a loan. The five cases in this fixture are adapted directly from those three vignettes, mapped onto the Case schema (id, intent, architecture, outcome_score, facts). The query is the physician vignette's new-problem side. The extraction is therefore "adapted" — the paper provides the scenarios in prose, not as structured feature vectors. The existing fixture in breed-inputs-real.ts uses a wholly fabricated 15-case IT-incident library and labels it only "inspired by" the paper; this extraction improves provenance by grounding cases in the paper's actual illustrative text.

input.intent: diagnose-and-treat current patient with fever and cough

cases.intent: patient treated two weeks ago with fever and cough
patient treated six months ago with fever and rash
first blowout — critical-pressure combination triggered well blow-out
second blowout — engineer error contributed to blow-out recurrence
previous company in similar financial trouble — loan refused

expected.retrieval_rationale: Highest Jaccard similarity: shares domain=medical, symptom_primary=fever, symptom_secondary=cough, urgency=moderate — 4 of 5 features match exactly (outcome_score 0.95).
expected.suggested_solution: antibiotic-course (copied from CASE-PHYSICIAN-2WK; no adaptation needed because all discriminating symptoms match)
expected.retain_action: Store current case as new entry in case base with confirmed outcome after treatment
expected.paper_statement: A physician — after having examined a particular patient — gets a reminding to a patient that he treated two weeks ago. Assuming that the reminding was caused by a similarity of important symptoms (and not the patient's hair-color, say), the physician uses the diagnosis and treatment of the previous patient to determine the disease and treatment for the patient in front of him. (Aamodt & Plaza 1994, p. 2)
